newsitem.title: USA: Eli Lilly posts record results on new drugs, Prozac.
newsitem.headline: Eli Lilly posts record results on new drugs, Prozac.

text.p: Eli Lilly & Co. Monday reported record fourth-quarter results, helped by major new product launches and Prozac, the world's most widely prescribed brand-name antidepressant.

Net income rose 20 percent to $373.0 million, or 68 cents a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $311.3 million, or 57 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Worldwide sales rose 15 percent to $2.06 billion from $1.80 billion.
Sale growth was partly offset by a 2 percent drop due to unfavourable exchange rate movements and a 3 percent reduction in global selling prices, Indianapolis-based Lilly said.
Full-year profits fell to $1.52 billion, or $2.78 a share, from $2.29 billion, or $4.03 a share, in 1995. Sales rose to $7.35 billion from $6.76 billion.
The company completed the divestiture of all its Medical Devices and Diagnostics Division subsidiaries in 1995, and the results do not include income from discontinued operations.
"The fourth quarter was marked by strong contributions both by Prozac and by four of our recently launched products: Gemzar, Humalog, ReoPro and Zyprexa," said Lilly Chairman Randall Tobias.
"We expect these new products to continue to build on their successful global launches as they help meet some of the world's urgent medical needs."

Gemzar is used to treat pancreatic cancer, Humalog is a fast-acting insulin for diabetics, ReoPro reduces the risk of heart attacks during angioplasty procedures and Zyprexa is a treatment for schizophrenia.
Tobias said Lilly's two other top priorities were to improve operating income growth while continuing to increase its commitment to research and development.

"The fourth-quarter results reflect our progress on these priorities as well, as operating income grew 19 percent in the fourth quarter while we were still able to fund a 23 percent increase in our research and development," he said.
Worldwide pharmaceutical sales and services for the quarter grew 15 percent to $1.887 billion.

Sales growth was led by Prozac, Humulin and three of the company's newer products, Gemzar, ReoPro and Zyprexa. The new products accounted for nearly two-thirds of the fourth-quarter sales growth, it said.

Increased health care management revenues was partly offset by lower sales of anti-infectives, Lilly said. Total U.S. pharmaceutical sales and services grew 24 percent from the 1995 fourth quarter. Overseas, pharmaceutical sales rose 2 percent with volume growth of 11 percent, but this was largely offset by unfavourable exchange rates and a reduction in selling prices, Lilly said.

Prozac sales rose 17 percent, to $603 million for the quarter as strong U.S. sales offset a drop in sales overseas due to competition from generic forms of Prozac in Canada and Australia and substantial competitive pressures in France.
Worldwide sales of animal health products grew 13 percent from the fourth quarter of 1995, Lilly said.
The company's stock fell $1.125 to $81.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
